item.media:description: Micron Technology union representatives gesture during a protest outside of the Micron facility demanding greater profit shares and better bonuses, in Taoyuan on October 22, 2026. item.title: Big Tech’s thirst for water is sparking a global resistance
item.dc:creator: Paris Marx
item.description: In his new book “Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires,” writer Paris Marx examines how local communities are resisting the growing demand for water to cool data centers.
item.content:encoded: After ChatGPT was released in November 2022, the tech industry was quick to herald the chatbot as the marker of a new wave of technological progress. As companies pushed to...
item.media:description: This photograph taken on September 6, 2026 shows a placard opposing data centers displayed on a water dispenser during the People's Convention on AI Data Centers event at Visakhapatnam in India's Andhra Pradesh state. Construction of a massive Google data centre in the Indian city of Visakhapatnam, often called Vizag, has been met with resistance from residents, who fear the impact on the environment and their lives. But the tech giant says its "gigawatt-scale" AI facility -- in southern Andhra Pradesh state, part of a $15 billion investment -- will use air cooling systems, and not water from an area already facing shortages. (Photo by Idrees MOHAMMED / AFP via Getty Images)
